correctness.rationale: For nonconstant trigonometric factor of degree d, a nonzero P(h)h′ has leading Laurent frequency (degP+1)d, ruling out cancellation and bounding outer degree. Normalize two affine freedoms of h: parameter dimension 2d−1, outer pair 2floor(n/d), so Dd=2d+2floor(n/d)−1. For 2≤d≤n−1, d+floor(n/d)≤n gives Dd≤2n−1. Degree d=n gives rank-one proportional L_n of dim2n+1; d=1 gives common odd-axis R_n of dim2n+1 via Chebyshev sin(ks)=sin(s)U_(k−1)(cos s). Distinct closed semialgebraic branches for n≥2; intersect in proportional odd polynomials, generic n sine coefficients + phase + scalar = n+2. No intermediate d can attain max dimension. At n=2 only d=1,2, hence C2=Ln ∪ Rn, and Fourier coefficient test handles zero first harmonics. Reviewed frozen CHECKER.py confirms sample phases/tangent directions and n≤200 inequality, but not infinite dimension proof.
